completion_definition: Completed means an initial curated cross-reference pass: the complete supplied English source unit and each retained target passage were read, and each pair has a specific explanation. It does not mean exhaustive coverage or independent specialist approval.

The communal prayer and personal assurance have different objects; the actual Matthew unit says evil, without an added one.

verses.text: Greet Prisca and Aquila and the household of Onesiphorus.
verses.display_text: Greet Prisca and Aquila and the household of Onesiphorus.

cross_references.rationale: Both greet the named Prisca and Aquila. Romans also names their work, risk and the Church in their house; Timothy's letter separately greets Onesiphorus's household. The two households are not merged.

target_verses.text: Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,
who risked their own neck for my life, to whom not only I give thanks, but also all the Churches of the Gentiles;
and greet the Church in their house. Greet Epaenetus my beloved, who is the firstfruits of Asia for Christ.

verses.text: Erastus remained in Corinth, but I left Trophimus sick in Miletus.
verses.display_text: Erastus remained in Corinth, but I left Trophimus sick in Miletus.

cross_references.rationale: Both name Trophimus in association with Paul. Acts explicitly calls him the Ephesian and describes seeing him with Paul; Timothy's letter names leaving him sick in Miletus. It does not date the sickness or make it the cause of the temple accusation, and supplies no new Erastus identity.

target_verses.text: For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city and supposed that Paul had brought him into the temple.

verses.text: The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you all.
verses.display_text: The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you all.

cross_references.rationale: Both close with the Lord, grace and the recipients' spirit in view. Galatians explicitly names our Lord Jesus Christ, brothers and Amen; Timothy's letter has the separate Lord-with-your-spirit and grace-with-you-all statements. Its shorter actual wording is not expanded.
